newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil extends latest rally.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil extends latest rally.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps extended its early day rally as fresh demand surfaced from players looking to hedge their physical sales on Tuesday as well others who expect a new round of physical buying on wednesday, traders said.
"The market is up sharply after yesterday's big physical purchase by Hin Leong and Sanko," brokers said.
The front month April gas oil was last quoted at $26.60/$26.80 per barrel, up from Tuesday's $26.00/$26.30, brokers said.
May gas oil was actively traded up as it became the centre of trading because the latest physical cargoes sold were mainly for early May lifting.
May was last quoted at $25.60/$25.80, from Tuesday's $24.90/$25.05, they said.
May traded earlier in the day at $25.40, $25.50, $25.60 and $25.68 per barrel, brokers said.
On Tuesday, Hin Leong and Sanko bought 1.35 million barrels with the bulk of it for May 4-8 lifting.
Since March 3, the two companies have bought more than 10 million barrels of gas oil for loading from end March to early May.
The April jet fuel/gas oil regrade widened futher after Tuesday's physical sell-off.
April regrade was last quoted at -$1.50/-$1.20 per barrel, from Tuesday's -$1.25/-$1.00, brokers said.

In the physical market, jet fuel traded at $24.75 per barrel, down about 30 cents from the last week's traded level. But on a cost-and-freight basis a 200,000-barrel cargo traded at $24.00 per barrel.
Fuel oil swaps steady after the recent rally with April swaps quoted at $98.50/$99.50 per tonne.
